correctness.rationale: Read the actual Case 3 hyperplane model and Theorem 6.3 of Avelin–Nedic arXiv:2610.04637v1: for pure q=a+b z_j, b>0, only j-hyperplane R_j≅R^{n−1} survives with measure bπ^{-(n−1)}ds, and its evaluation vectors reduce after cancellation to ∏_{k≠j}(s_k−conj(z_k))^{-1}. In one variable these Cauchy kernels are the Hardy H²(C_+) boundary reproducing kernels, whose closed span is all H² by the RKHS property. The finite products span the Hilbert tensor product of the n−1 Hardy factors by density of algebraic tensor products; this proves exact vector-cyclic core. In each L²(R) factor the opposite Hardy space is an infinite-dimensional orthogonal complement by Paley–Wiener. Tensoring an opposite-Hardy vector with nonzero L² vectors in other factors embeds infinite-dimensional orthogonal complement for every n≥2. This is only a vector span and does not show invariant/reducing subspace for self-adjoint relations.
residual_risks: The conjugate parameter convention is crucial: use z in the upper half-plane so poles lie in the lower half-plane.
Vector cyclicity alone is weaker than minimal self-adjoint relation representation; do not conflate them.
